rows.stem: Yeast multiplies by which of the following methods ?
rows.solution:
In yeast a small bud grows out of the parent cell. The nucleus divides and one part passes into the bud, which then detaches and grows into a new yeast cell. This is budding. (Binary fission is seen in Amoeba and multiple fission in Plasmodium.)

This is option (D) Budding.

rows.stem:
The reasons for excessive generation of wastes are :

(i) Use and throw policy.

(ii) Increased availability of packaged food.

(iii) Increased construction wastes.

(iv) Non-sorting of dry and wet wastes.
rows.solution:
All four add to the waste we generate. A use-and-throw lifestyle discards things that could be reused, packaged food brings a large amount of packing material, construction produces large amounts of debris, and when dry and wet wastes are not sorted, little of the waste can be recycled or composted, so more of it piles up.

This is option (C) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Bacteria produced as a result of asexual reproduction would be similar.

**Reason (R) :** There would be only minor differences between the bacteria generated due to small inaccuracies in DNA replication.
rows.context: Question No. 8 & 9 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
In asexual reproduction a single parent copies its DNA and passes it on, so the bacteria produced are very similar to the parent and to each other, and the Assertion is true. DNA copying is not perfectly accurate, so small inaccuracies give rise to minor differences, and the Reason is true. Since only minor differences arise, the bacteria remain similar, so the Reason explains the Assertion.

Both are true and the Reason is the correct explanation, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
Given below is a diagrammatic representation of cross-section of a leaf :

(i) Identify ‘P’ in the given diagram and write down its role in plants.

(ii) Write down a balanced equation of process of photo-synthesis.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (i) asks to identify the part labelled P on the printed drawing of a leaf cross-section: an upper row of flat epidermal cells, below it a row of tall column-shaped cells packed with small oval bodies (the label P points at one of those bodies inside a column cell), loosely packed rounded cells beneath (label Q points into that layer; Q is not asked about), and a lower epidermis. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
(i) P is a chloroplast (one of the small oval bodies packed in the column-shaped palisade cells). Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light energy; they are the site of photosynthesis, where this energy is used to make food (glucose) from carbon dioxide and water.

(ii) \(\mathrm{6CO_2 + 12H_2O \xrightarrow[\text{Sunlight}]{\text{Chlorophyll}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 + 6H_2O}\)

The product \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) is glucose. (The equation is balanced: 6 carbon, 24 hydrogen and 24 oxygen atoms on each side.)

rows.stem:
(a) Mention the gland and the hormone secreted by it in scary situation in human beings.

(b) Write two responses that enable the human body to be ready to deal with such situation.
rows.solution:
(a) The adrenal gland secretes the hormone adrenaline in a scary situation.

(b) Any two:

1. Adrenaline acts on the heart, which beats faster to supply more oxygen to the muscles.

2. The blood supply to the skin and the digestive system is reduced, because the small arteries there contract (the muscles around them contract), so more blood is diverted to the skeletal muscles.

3. The breathing rate increases because of contractions of the diaphragm and the rib muscles.

rows.stem: In the following diagram, if acetic acid of same concentration is taken in place of dilute sulphuric acid, then

options.label: A
options.text: Same amount of \(\mathrm{H_2}\) gas will be evolved.

options.label: C
options.text: The amount of \(\mathrm{H_2}\) gas evolved in less amount.

options.label: D
options.text: In place of \(\mathrm{H_2}\) gas, \(\mathrm{O_2}\) gas will be evolved.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the stem says 'In the following diagram' and names only the acid; the metal comes from the drawing alone: a test tube on a stand holding zinc granules in dilute sulphuric acid with hydrogen gas bubbles, a delivery tube leading into a trough of soap solution, soap bubbles filled with hydrogen rising, and a hand holding a candle to a bubble ('Burning of hydrogen gas with a pop sound'). The English page prints it in greyscale; the Hindi page idx 13 prints the same drawing in colour with Hindi labels. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
In the drawing, zinc granules react with dilute sulphuric acid and the hydrogen given off fills the soap bubbles:

\(\mathrm{Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2}\)

Acetic acid also reacts with zinc to give hydrogen:

\(\mathrm{Zn + 2CH_3COOH \rightarrow (CH_3COO)_2Zn + H_2}\)

But acetic acid is a weak acid. At the same concentration it is only slightly ionised, so it gives far fewer \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions than sulphuric acid, and hydrogen is evolved more slowly and in a smaller amount. (Oxygen is never a product of a metal reacting with an acid.)

This is option (C) The amount of \(\mathrm{H_2}\) gas evolved in less amount.

rows.stem: On reaction with dilute \(\mathrm{HCl}\), which of the following pair of metals will evolve hydrogen gas ?
rows.solution:
A metal displaces hydrogen from dilute hydrochloric acid only if it is more reactive than hydrogen. Magnesium and aluminium lie above hydrogen in the activity series:

\(\mathrm{Mg + 2HCl \rightarrow MgCl_2 + H_2}\)

\(\mathrm{2Al + 6HCl \rightarrow 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2}\)

Copper and silver lie below hydrogen and do not react with dilute HCl, so every pair containing one of them is ruled out.

This is option (D) magnesium and aluminium.

rows.stem: How is a universal indicator obtained ? How is the wide range of pH of solution tested by it ?
rows.solution:
A universal indicator is obtained by mixing several indicators.

Because it is a mixture, it shows a different colour at each concentration of hydrogen ions in a solution. A few drops of it are added to the solution, and the colour it turns is matched against the colour chart supplied with it, which gives the pH of the solution anywhere on the scale from 0 to 14.

rows.stem:
What happens when

(i) Calcium carbonate is heated ?

(ii) Silver bromide is exposed to sunlight ?

(iii) Lead is added to copper (II) chloride solution ?

Write balanced chemical equations of the reactions involved in support of your answer.
rows.solution:
(i) Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating to calcium oxide (quick lime) and carbon dioxide. This is a thermal decomposition reaction.

\(\mathrm{CaCO_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} CaO(s) + CO_2(g)}\)

(ii) Silver bromide decomposes in sunlight to silver and bromine; the pale yellow solid turns grey. This is a photolytic decomposition reaction (it is used in black and white photography).

\(\mathrm{2AgBr(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Br_2(g)}\)

(iii) Lead is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper(II) chloride solution. This is a displacement reaction.

\(\mathrm{Pb(s) + CuCl_2(aq) \rightarrow PbCl_2(aq) + Cu(s)}\)

rows.stem:
(a) Define absolute refractive index of an optical medium.

(b)

| Material Medium | Refractive Index |
|---|---|
| A | 1.50 |
| B | 1.46 |
| C | 1.31 |
| D | 1.77 |

Arrange these material mediums given in the table in increasing order of speed of light through them.
rows.solution:
(a) The absolute refractive index of a medium is the ratio of the speed of light in air (strictly, vacuum) to the speed of light in that medium: \(n = \frac{c}{v}\).

(b) Since \(v = \frac{c}{n}\), the higher the refractive index, the lower the speed of light. In decreasing order of refractive index the media are D (1.77), A (1.50), B (1.46), C (1.31), so the speed of light increases in the same order:

\(v_D < v_A < v_B < v_C\)

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. Use lens formula to determine the position of the image. What will be the size of the image in this case ?
rows.solution:
For a convex lens, \(u = -30\) cm and \(f = +15\) cm. By the lens formula:

\(\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}\), so \(\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{-30} = \frac{2 - 1}{30} = \frac{1}{30}\)

\(v = +30\) cm. The image is formed 30 cm behind the lens, on the other side from the object.

Magnification: \(m = \frac{v}{u} = \frac{+30}{-30} = -1\).

So the image is the same size as the object (real and inverted). This is expected: the object is at \(2F_1\) (twice the focal length), so the image forms at \(2F_2\), with the same size.

rows.stem:
(i) List any two features of the electric current used in the houses of India.

(ii) Write any two differences between direct current and an alternating current.

(iii) How will you identify live wire and neutral wire in a domestic electric circuit ?
rows.solution:
(i) Any two features of the current supplied to our houses:

1. It is alternating current: its direction changes periodically.

2. Its frequency is 50 Hz.

3. The potential difference between the live wire and the neutral wire is 220 V.

(ii) Any two differences:

| Direct current | Alternating current |
|---|---|
| It flows in one direction only. | It reverses its direction periodically. |
| Its sources are cells and batteries. | It is supplied by power plants (AC generators). |

(iii) The live wire has red insulation and the neutral wire has black insulation. (A line tester also glows when it touches the live wire and not the neutral wire.)

rows.stem:
(i) Why is fuse an important component in our electric circuits ?

(ii) Distinguish between overloading and short-circuiting of a circuit.

(iii) Giving reason explain what type of materials are used in fuse wires.
rows.solution:
(i) A fuse is a safety device. When an unduly high current flows because of overloading or a short circuit, the fuse wire heats up, melts and breaks the circuit, so the electric appliances and the circuit are protected from damage (and from fire).

(ii)

| Overloading | Short-circuiting |
|---|---|
| It happens when too many appliances are connected to a single socket, so the circuit draws more current than it is meant to carry. It can also happen through an accidental hike in the supply voltage. | It happens when the live wire comes into direct contact with the neutral wire (for example when the insulation is damaged), so the resistance becomes very small and the current rises sharply. |

(iii) A fuse wire is a piece of wire made of a metal or an alloy of appropriate (low) melting point, such as an alloy of tin and lead. The low melting point makes it melt as soon as the current exceeds the safe value, so it breaks the circuit before the other wires and the appliances are damaged.
